description: Records each Claude Code subagent start with o-lane agent-hook, so lanes associated with that agent show its live state. Added beside existing SubagentStart entries, never replacing them.

name: Claude Code instructions note
description: Adds the 'Tracking work (o-lane)' note to Claude Code's user instructions, between o-lane markers; the rest of the file is untouched.
content:
## Tracking work (o-lane)

Track the work you do for the owner as lanes in o-lane, not as mtm tasks: mtm tasks are the owner's, and you create or edit them only when the owner asks. Every lane belongs to a project: use the matching mtm project (`mtm project list`), and if none fits, create one (`mtm project new NAME --dir DIR`) rather than leaving lanes unscoped. Make one root lane per owner request, with the owner's words as its wording (`o-lane lane define --project PROJECT --lanes '[...]'`, or `o-lane plan define` from a plan's Lanes table), and a child lane per piece of work. Set each lane's state as it moves (planned, running, review, merged, done, parked, cancelled) with `o-lane lane state`, and associate a lane with the pane that runs it (`o-lane lane associate --pane WINDOW_ID`) so the owner's Lanes page shows live state. Use the mtm MCP gateway when it is available (`run` with `lane.lane define`, `lane.lane state`, `lane.lane associate`, and `md.doc new` for docs); otherwise the CLI. Write findings and reports as a Markdown doc linked to the lane; use notes only for short jots.

Keep lane states true; the main (coordinating) agent owns this for every lane it started or delegated:
- Create the root and child lanes when the work starts, not afterwards, and set `running` and associate the pane in the same step.
- `running` means an agent is working on it right now in an associated pane. When that stops, change the state before ending your turn: `review` (work exists but is not merged: name the branch), `merged`, `done`, `parked` (paused or waiting: say on what) or `cancelled`. Give the reason with `--note`; it shows as the lane's reason on the Lanes page.
- A pane belongs to one lane: associate it with the lane it now works on, and o-lane moves it off the old one.
- At session start, before a handoff, and when the owner asks, reconcile: every `running` lane (`o-lane lane list --state running`) must have an associated pane whose agent is working (`tuios list-windows -s SESSION --json`: `agent_state`); fix any that don't, with a note saying what was found. Update the parent when all its children have moved.

name: Codex instructions note
description: Adds the same note to Codex's user instructions. Both items share one marker pair, so when both paths are the same file the note appears once.
